clue.text: Harm poet? This blunder might well

parts.note: the two words are the letters of a figure of speech (M, E, T, A, P, H, O, R) jumbled, so they are that word mixed up

explanation.surface: A clumsy image in a poem could well damage its poet's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, a 'mixed' version of METAPHOR, and you get HARM POET. The rest says such a blunder might well do so.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining incompatible images, like 'nip it in the bud before it snowballs', is a recognised stylistic error.

clue.text: Green parts within tattoo an unseemly thing

parts.note: in means within

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so green goes into the middle of tattoo

parts.note: to tattoo is to drum, rapping out a rhythm
eco is a prefix meaning green or environmental

explanation.surface: Body art with green bits is something unbecoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tattoo' suggests body art, but it is a drumbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper or unseemly behaviour, a lack of propriety.

clue.text: Wise bird one's taken in

indicators.note: taken in means one goes inside the bird

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clever bird has been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like an adjective, but it is the surname of comedian Ernie Wise of the British double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's first name pairs with his surname Wise to give the famous entertainer.

clue.text: Sun about to end wet period

parts.note: when Sunday finishes, Monday follows, abbreviated Mon
about to end means coming shortly, soon

explanation.surface: The sun will soon be gone, bringing rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sun about to end' as days: when Sunday is about to end, it will be MON SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal rains of South Asia come as a prolonged wet season.

clue.text: Left holding aid for driver turning tip of plane?

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembly is read backwards
holding means the left side keeps the golf aid inside

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a golfer tees the ball up before hitting it with a driver

explanation.surface: A pilot turning a plane while gripping something to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests aircraft, but it is the plane tree; 'driver' is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a plane tree is its crown or uppermost branches.

clue.text: Dives where copper arrests lout wasted on grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
arrests means the policeman holds the yob inside

parts.note: PC is a police constable

indicators.note: wasted, drunk, means the letters of lout are scrambled

parts.note: a rat is an informer, a grass

explanation.surface: A policeman nicks a drunk yob on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus, not someone diving.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical rich man is a byword for wealth, so he is a type of the very rich.

clue.text: It's commonly like decimal

definitions.meaning: decimal counting is in base ten, read as two words

explanation.surface: Something is commonly compared to a decimal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done frequently is done repeatedly; and decimal means based on ten.

clue.text: Passing quality ball, guys on pitch cool amid chaos

indicators.note: amid means the other pieces sit in the middle of the chaos

parts.note: a mess is a state of chaos

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means one piece is placed above the next

parts.note: O is ball-shaped
men are guys
tar is pitch
in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A footballer with class on the pitch keeping calm amid the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface misleads: 'Passing' means transient, not passing the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleeting or transient nature is the state of lasting only an instant.

clue.text: Sex maniac, due for treatment, accepting hospital's miracle solution

indicators.note: accepting means the jumbled letters take in the hospital
for treatment means the letters are reworked, as if being treated

explanation.surface: A sex fiend, due a cure, is admitted to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Latin for 'god from the machine', an improbable device resolving a plot.

clue.text: Uncovered more steps to secure home rule

indicators.note: uncovered means the word more loses its outer letters, its cover
to secure means the steps hold the home inside them

parts.note: a dance is a set of steps
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone who found more stairs is told to secure a house rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or regulation, a synonym for a rule.

clue.text: For Wenger, a match is free

parts.note: Arsène Wenger, the French football manager, would say 'un' for 'a'
a cup tie is a match

explanation.surface: A football match is free for the famous Arsenal manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsène Wenger, Arsenal's long-serving French manager, signals French: 'a' becomes UN. The football surface makes TIE natural, as in a cup tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a knot is to release or liberate something, so the verb works as a synonym.

clue.text: Party leader seems clever, not at all odd

indicators.note: not at all odd means take only the even letters of the words seems clever

explanation.surface: A political leader appears smart and perfectly normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' suggests politics, but it is the host who leads a party's entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies presides over a gathering's proceedings, introducing acts and keeping things moving.

clue.text: Payments from friendly society

parts.note: an outgoing person is sociable and friendly

explanation.surface: Money paid out by a mutual benefit association.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'friendly society' is a British mutual insurance association, but here the two words split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are expenditure, the sums of money a person or business spends.

clue.text: Fine, entertaining line that re-starts play

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so fine takes in the line

parts.note: thin means fine, as in a fine thread
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A good, amusing line that gets a drama going again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests theatre, but this is the football restart from the touchline.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, when the ball crosses the touchline the game resumes with a throw back onto the pitch.

clue.text: Women have to eat blind drunk, having had buffets

indicators.note: to eat means the women and have take in the jumbled letters

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of blind reel about

explanation.surface: Women have a drink before eating after enjoying buffet meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffets' suggests food, but it means blows from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To be buffeted is to be struck repeatedly by gusts, leaving one dishevelled by the wind.

clue.text: US criminal law to mystify

parts.note: perp is American slang for a perpetrator, a criminal
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: American criminal law is designed to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle or bewilder someone is to baffle them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Reds can prefer heartless, wicked uprising

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, the loo

indicators.note: heartless means the word prefer loses everything inside its outer letters

parts.note: evil means wicked

explanation.surface: Communists may prefer a heartless, wicked revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds' suggests communists, but it is the nickname of Liverpool Football Club.
explanation.definitionFit: The English football club plays in red shirts and is nicknamed after that colour.

clue.text: Men turning crazy like Caligula …?

indicators.note: turning means the letters for men are read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means the ordinary soldiers, the men
manic means wild or crazy

explanation.surface: Soldiers going mad like the notorious Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Caligula was an emperor of Rome, so he is of Rome or Roman in character.

clue.text: Shipping company downsized in style

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew
cut means reduced or downsized

explanation.surface: A shipping firm has slimmed down in fashionable fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, bristly haircut is a hairstyle.

clue.text: … or this lady who's wonderful company, swigging much wine back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse
swigging means drinking, so the company takes the wine inside

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
a vat holds a large quantity of wine

explanation.surface: A woman who is great company, knocking back plenty of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 18 across: like Caligula, or like this lady, both Roman. A1 (top-notch) is spelt AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavia, sister of Augustus and wife of Mark Antony, was a famous Roman woman.

clue.text: Dickens's Newgate?

definitions.meaning: the dickens is an old euphemism for the devil
Newgate was a London prison long ago, nick being slang for jail

explanation.surface: The prison Charles Dickens wrote about.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil has the traditional nickname of the old fellow Nick; Newgate was a jail of former times.

clue.text: Beak's outpouring, having seen bold criminal swallowing drug

indicators.note: swallowing means the jumbled letters take another piece inside
criminal signals the words seen bold are to be treated wrongly, jumbled

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A magistrate's outburst after seeing a brazen offender taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate, fitting the court surface, but here it means a nose. 'Criminal' jumbles SEEN BOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is slang for a nose, and blood flowing from it is a nasal haemorrhage.

clue.text: Repeated appeal about line in dance music

indicators.note: about means the doubled letters go around the line
repeated means the abbreviation for appeal is written twice

parts.note: SA is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A recurring plea about a line in a song for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin American genre is lively music played for dancing.

clue.text: Mathematical area returning height measurements

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but taken in the sense of a person's size around the middle

indicators.note: returning means the word for the maths subject comes back, reversed

parts.note: trig is short for trigonometry

explanation.surface: A branch of maths giving back the readings of how tall things are.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the distance around something, a person's waist size being part of their vital statistics.

clue.text: Keep chattering where French is spoken by Africans

definitions.text: where French is spoken by Africans

parts.note: to gab is to chatter
on means continuing, as in keep on

explanation.surface: Talking constantly in a French-speaking part of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep chattering' reads as GAB ON, carry on talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central African republic was a French colony and French is its official language.

clue.text: Getting end away, soothe love's fire

indicators.note: getting end away means losing the final letter of the word for soothe

parts.note: to salve is to soothe
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a lover's passion being calmed after a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex, a saucy surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of fire.

clue.text: Conservative member miserable in U-turn

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
down means depressed or miserable

explanation.surface: A Tory MP unhappy about a reversal of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat from a stated position is a reversal, as when a government backs down.

clue.text: Reward's collected in wagering pound with care

indicators.note: collected means gathered up, so the reward holds the other pieces

parts.note: pay is a reward for work
staking means betting or wagering
L is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A prize gathered in a careful bet of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something meticulously and diligently, taking pains, is doing it carefully.
